scope_statement: Full-scope verdict on the declared L0 acceptance tests and the A0 hard-failure taxonomy as applied to a ledger record: class binding, verification vocabulary, conclusion-inflation controls, source linkage, unresolved honesty, HF-14/HF-01, grounding. It does not re-page-check the quoted theorems; L1's independent re-fetch spot checks at audit 315c19145065 are the separate locator-level evidence.

findings.finding: HF-14 self_certified_acceptance fires at this hash: 60/62 rows set status=accepted (50) or supports_claim=true (60, overlap 50) and the frozen row schema contains no reviewer / verdict / artifact-hash key, so no row can satisfy the detector's evidentiary requirement. evaluation_rubric.yaml HF-14 is severity=critical and its detector text is explicitly ledger-inclusive ("a ledger or claim record ... with no independent reviewer verdict field and no artifact hash"), and the rubric states a critical HF cannot be accepted regardless of other merits. First affected rows: D-001, D-002, D-003; the rubric's own evidence line names T-201..T-203, which remain in this state.

Adjudication trail (recorded for the controller, not an excuse): an earlier pass of this same review checked 13 ledger-discipline dimensions and returned accept because none of them covered HF-14. Independent reviews reviews/L0-review-21.json (score 3.0) and reviews/L0-review-22.json (score 2.0) flagged HF-14 at the same hash; reviews/L0-review-032.json treats the sibling HF-01 item as a claim-vocabulary collision to be deferred. Re-reading the frozen detector text, the ledger-inclusive reading is the plain one, so this review returns revise. The correction is recorded rather than silently dropped: the accept version was never emitted to the outbox.

HF-01 (theorem without artifact_refs) is reported but not counted as a hard failure here: 30 rows carry conclusion_type=theorem with no artifact binding. HF-01's detector is claim-scoped (`claim.conclusion_type == theorem AND ...`), and the map has the ledger-scope question under adjudication (worker-032 N-C5; lead disposition deferred to a bounded rev 3). If the controller rules that ledger theorem rows are claims, HF-01 also fires as critical.

Status/resolution coherence: 13 accepted rows keep an item in unresolved[] that reads as acceptance-qualifying (peer review / refereeing / publication status), e.g. T-206, T-207, T-208, T-301, T-515, T-517. Under the reading status=ledger-admission this is a display issue; under the reading status=result-acceptance it is flash-22's evidence_strength_mismatch. The field's meaning should be pinned in the revision.

Ledger-discipline checks all pass at the pinned hashes: 62 rows >= 15; unique theorem_ids; all required fields present; every class_ids token is one of the frozen four and every non-class token sits in ledger_tags; verification_status vocabulary legal. These are the dimensions that were already repaired in this revision and they hold.

Verification depth is honest and not inflated: 61 rows abstract-read, 1 unverified, 0 full-text/page-checked; the citation registry's evidence_type for cited sources is abstract/metadata, matching. Source linkage is reciprocal in both directions (no unknown source_ids, no row without an audit link), and SRC-090 (registry-unresolved) is cited by no row.

Non-blocking provenance echo gap: 3 rows do not repeat the citation-registry metadata corrections they depend on indirectly - T-103 (SRC-016 quote symbol fidelity), T-505 (SRC-025 year vs publisher year), T-510 (SRC-050 venue page range). None carries the row's mathematical claim; T-201 explicitly repairs the substantive SRC-041/054 identifier split.

Independent grounding spot check: for every strong row, content-token overlap of statement_exact against the cited sources' recorded title+excerpt is >= 0.174 (lowest D-009); no strong row below the 0.15 follow-up threshold. This measures lexical grounding only and does not substitute for page-level verification.

falsifier: At the pinned hashes this revise turns to accept if the controller adjudicates HF-14 as claim-scoped-only (so a ledger row need not carry a reviewer/artifact field) AND HF-01 is likewise ruled claim-scoped. Alternatively, a new revision that pins the meaning of status, adds reviewer/artifact-hash provenance and re-passes these checks is reviewable at its own hash. A change to either pinned hash voids this binding.
